name: Cheesy salmon & broccoli egg bake

source.author: Instagram (English, pasted text)
source.notes: Cubed fresh salmon and blanched broccoli in a dish, covered with an egg + cream custard, topped with halved cherry tomatoes and shredded mozzarella, baked 190°C 25–30 min. Analyzed as 4 servings; eggs taken as 5.5 (the post says 5–6), mozzarella as standard (not light), salmon as farmed Atlantic. Estimate.

steps: Preheat to 190 °C and line a baking dish.
Boil the broccoli 3–4 min in salted water; drain well.
Spread broccoli and salmon cubes in the dish.
Whisk eggs, cream, salt, pepper and oregano; pour over.
Top with halved cherry tomatoes and the mozzarella.
Bake 25–30 min until set, salmon cooked through and the top golden. Cool slightly before slicing.

batch_totals.note: Whole bake (4 servings). Very low carb, high protein; fat is substantial but a big share is salmon's omega-3s. The full-fat mozzarella is the one place the fat is 'empty' — the obvious lever.

him.verdict: A nutrient-dense bake: ~32 g protein per serving with a big dose of omega-3 EPA/DHA and vitamin D from the salmon (both sperm-priority micros), plus selenium from eggs + salmon and vitamin C from broccoli. Fat is high (~27 g), but much of it is the good kind; the 150 g of full-fat mozzarella is the avoidable part. Swap to light mozzarella / halve it and it's a 9.
flags: ~32 g protein, very low carb (~6 g)
~1.1 g omega-3 + ~300 IU vitamin D per serving (sperm micros)
high fat (~27 g) — salmon (good) + full-fat mozzarella (lever)
suggested_mods: Use light mozzarella or halve it (~75 g) — saves ~45 kcal / ~4 g fat per serving
Skip the cream (milk or nothing) — eggs set fine on their own
Double the broccoli for more fibre and volume

her_preconception.verdict: Close to ideal for her: salmon is low-mercury and a top DHA + vitamin D source, eggs bring choline, broccoli adds folate + vitamin C, mozzarella adds calcium — all fully baked. Just make sure the salmon and eggs are cooked through (set custard, opaque salmon).
prenatal_highlights: DHA + vitamin D (salmon) — fetal brain development

safety_advisories.note: Bake until the custard is fully set and the salmon is opaque throughout — no runny egg or undercooked fish in pregnancy.
safety_advisories.swap: add a few minutes if the centre is soft

suggested_mods: No changes needed — a strong prenatal dish

cooking_guide: Drain the blanched broccoli very well (even pat it dry) — wet broccoli makes the custard watery.
Cut the salmon into even ~2–3 cm cubes so it cooks at the same rate as the custard sets.
Season the egg mix properly — eggs need salt to taste of anything — but go lighter if using salty cheese.
Spread everything in a single even layer so the custard surrounds it rather than pooling.
Bake until the centre is set (no wobble) and a knife comes out clean; check at 25 min.
Rest 5 min before slicing so it holds together.
